newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher in technical bounce.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher in technical bounce.

text.p: Argentine bonds were firmer late Monday as a technical bounce aided by a rise on Wall Street took the market higher amid thin activity.
One trader said volume was "ridiculously thin," evidencing that most players remained on the sidelines in anticipation of Tuesday's U.S. consumer prices report.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 3/8 at 89, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was unchanged at 124.65.
Traders said there was uncertainty about the market's likely reaction to a negative figure in Tuesday's consumer price report.
"I do not think the market has a lot more to fall even if the figure is very bad," said another trader. He admitted, however, that he had a flat position going into the report.
The problem, said traders, is that if the figure shows clearly rising U.S. inflation, it will create more uncertainty about how much the Federal Reserve is likely to raise rates.
Call money rose to 5.93 percent from 5.83 percent.
